info.title: ShipBlu Support: the myBlu ticket API
info.description:
The HTTP API the myBlu app reaches support through, and the webhook it is told of replies by. The guide, `docs/myblu-api.md` in the shipblu-support repository, says what every field means, what an SDK must do, and the scenarios it is checked with; this document is the shapes.

Two planes. The **server plane** is myBlu's backend, holding `MYBLU_API_TOKEN`: it mints and ends sessions and does nothing else. The **client plane** is the app, through the SDK, holding a session token for one user: it does everything else, as that user.

Every client-plane request carries `ShipBlu-Client`. Every answer carries `ShipBlu-Request-Id` and `Cache-Control: no-store`. JSON, UTF-8, ISO-8601 instants in UTC, UUID ids, no credential in a URL and no trailing slash.

**It changes by addition.** Fields and enum values appear without notice, and a client ignores a field it does not know and keeps an enum value it does not know. What an operation sends and answers is fixed from the release that ships it; a breaking change is `/api/v2`. Each change is a dated line in `docs/myblu-api-changelog.md`, whose newest date is `info.version`.

servers.description: Production, on the name meant to last. Kept in the app’s build configuration.
Production, on its service host: the same server.
Staging: suspended, and resumed for named test windows with its own secrets. Never point a staging app at production.

post.summary: Mint a session for one user
post.description:
Server plane: myBlu's backend, when its app asks for support, never the app. Mints a new token on every call; the backend hands it to the app and keeps no copy. Twenty-four hours, no refresh: the app asks its backend again.

Served from stage 3. Until that stage ships, the path answers `404` with no body of this shape: the shapes are published first so the app and the SDK can be written against them.

mint.summary: A user signed in on iOS

400.description: Refused as written. `invalid_request`: a field or a header is wrong; `field` names it when one is to blame. The backend's own bug: it answers its app with a `502` of its own.

401.description: Not authenticated. `unauthenticated`: no bearer, a malformed one, or one that is not `MYBLU_API_TOKEN` as this server holds it. The backend's own bug, with no session behind it to refresh: never retried, and answered to the app with a `502` of the backend's own.

403.description: Forbidden. `blocked`: the user may not use support, and nothing was minted. Relayed to the app as it came, status and body, and its SDK stops there: never retried.

429.description: Too many requests. `rate_limited`: the server plane, or this user's minting, is over its limit. Relayed to the app as it came, `Retry-After` included, and its SDK waits that long; the backend does not wait it out itself.

500.description: Failed on the server. `internal`: a failure on the server. Answered to the app with a `502` of the backend's own, and the app asks again on its next foreground.

503.description: Not available here. `not_configured`: the API is not switched on here, and nothing was minted. Relayed to the app as it came, and its SDK holds its outbox until the next foreground: never retried.

post.summary: End every session of one user
post.description:
Server plane. Ends every session of `externalUserId` on every device, and records why. Answers `204` whether or not the user is known, so it cannot be used to ask who is.

post.summary: Something happened on one of the user's tickets
post.description:
Sent to myBlu's backend, at the one URL it registered, so it can push: `message.created` when a person on the team or an automated reply writes on one of the user's tickets (from stage 6), and `survey.created` when a resolved ticket's survey is ready (from stage 8). Ids only, never text: read the message or the survey through the client plane. A hint, not the truth; the poll is the truth. More types are added; answer `2xx` to one you do not know.

The URL is `https`, with no query string and no userinfo; one that is not is refused when it is first used, and nothing is sent. It is posted to exactly as registered and a redirect is not followed, so a `3xx` is a failed delivery: register it as the receiver serves it, trailing slash included. Each attempt waits ten seconds for an answer, and one not answered by then is retried as a refusal is. Retries back off and stop within a day of the event, so a day of dedupe on `id` covers them; a receiver down for longer loses those pushes, never the messages, which the app's poll still reads.

The signature is `X-ShipBlu-Signature`, an HMAC under `MYBLU_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; the guide prints the scheme, the receiver's rules and a test vector.

survey.created.summary: A survey on a resolved ticket

2XX.description: Received. Answer within ten seconds, as soon as the signature is checked and the event recorded, and do the work after: anything else, a redirect included, is retried with backoff, and the same event arrives again.

TicketStatus.description: The ticket's state. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know; a client draws one it does not know as it draws `open`. `resolved` takes a reply, which reopens the ticket; `closed` does not.

MessageFrom.description: Who wrote the message: `customer` is the user, `agent` a person on the support team, `system` nobody (an automated reply). Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know; a client draws one it does not know as `system`, which claims nobody wrote it.

SurveyStatus.description: `sent`: waiting for a rating. `answered`: rated, and a comment may still be added. `expired`: can no longer be answered. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know; a client treats one it does not know as `expired`.

id.description: The attachment; `GET /attachments/{id}` gives a link to its bytes.

filename.description: The name it was sent under, cleaned of anything a path could use.

contentType.description: What the server read from the bytes, never what the sender labelled them.

Attachment.description: A file on a message, in the order it was sent.

id.description: The message. Merge by it: a page may repeat a row the client already holds.

text.description: Words somebody wrote, never a label of ours: `""` for a message sent as files alone.

clientId.description: The `Idempotency-Key` the user's own message was sent under, on every read and not only the send's answer, so an outbox matches a message whose answer was lost. Null on a message the user did not send.

attachments.description: Files on the message, in order; empty when there are none.

Message.description: One message on a ticket. Only replies are ever returned: never a note, an event or a forward.

text.description: Its text, or its first 140 UTF-16 code units when longer, as JavaScript's `length` counts — one fewer where the 140th would split a surrogate pair, so it never ends in half a character. `""` for a message sent as files alone.

Preview.description: The ticket's newest message, for a list row.

TicketSurveySummary.description: Whether the ticket has a survey, so a list can prompt without a call per ticket; `GET /tickets/{id}/survey` reads it whole. Always null until the survey's stage ships.

number.description: The number an agent and the user can both quote.

subject.description: The opening message's first words; null when it had none, such as a ticket opened with a photo, and the app draws its own title.

anyOf.description: A tracking number the ticket is about, as the app shows it: 1 to 64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 -`. Stored as sent and returned to this user only.

trackingNumber.description: The tracking number the ticket was opened with, as sent, or null. Never one an agent added.

statusLabel.description: A label the support team typed for this status, in one language, shown as written; null when there is none, and the client uses its own word for `status`.

canReply.description: Whether a message may be sent on it now; false once it is `closed`.

lastMessageAt.description: When its newest message was stored; the list is ordered by it.

unreadCount.description: The team's messages on it the user has not marked read.

preview.description: The ticket's newest message, for a list row; null only for a ticket with no message the app may read.

Ticket.description: A ticket the signed-in user opened from the app.

online.description: Whether the support team is working now, by its own hours.

opensAt.description: When it next opens, while it is closed; null while it is open or when the team's hours are not set.

timezone.description: The IANA zone the team's hours are kept in, e.g. `Africa/Cairo`; null when its hours are not set.

SupportHours.description: The support team's hours, for a line such as "we reply from 9:00".

id.description: The signed-in user's id here, which a contact merge does not change. A client keeps it in the store it namespaces by `externalId`; when it changes, the user's identity here was removed and made again, and the client wipes its cached tickets and messages.

externalId.description: The id myBlu's backend minted the session for. A client that asked for another user discards the token.

canCreate.description: Whether `POST /tickets` is open now; when false, hide the new-ticket button.

maxOpen.description: How many open or pending tickets one user may have at once.

messageMaxChars.description: The longest message text, in UTF-16 code units.

maxFiles.description: The most files on one message.

maxFileBytes.description: The largest one file, in bytes.

maxTotalBytes.description: The largest all of one message's files together, in bytes.

contentTypes.description: The `Content-Type` labels a file part may carry.

extensions.description: The filename extensions, without the dot, that admit a file labelled `application/octet-stream` or not at all.

limits.description: What a send may carry. They move with the server, so a client checks against these rather than numbers of its own.

support.description: The support team's hours. Absent until the stage that carries them ships; a client draws nothing for it then.

threadSeconds.description: Seconds between polls of an open thread, until an answer says otherwise. At least 1.

listSeconds.description: Seconds between polls of the ticket list, until an answer says otherwise. At least 1.

polling.description: What a screen polls at before its first answer's `pollAfterSeconds`.

Config.description: Who is signed in and what the server allows, read on start and after every new token.

rating.description: The rating kept, 1 to 5; null until rated.

comment.description: The comment kept; null until one is added.

locale.description: The language the survey is worded in, which can differ from the app's. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know.

intro.description: A first line, such as "Your ticket is resolved."

labels.description: Five words for the ratings 1 to 5, in order: very bad, bad, okay, good, great.

commentMaxChars.description: The longest comment kept, in UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts: stop the comment box there. A longer comment is `400 invalid_request`, never cut short. On the survey, beside the box's other words, so a client checks against this rather than a number of its own.

thanks.description: What to show once it is answered.

expiresAt.description: When it can no longer be answered; null when it does not lapse.

Survey.description: The satisfaction survey on a resolved ticket, worded on the server. The first rating wins whichever way it came, so draw the rating this returns, not the one tapped.

token.description: The session token, `sbu_` and then an opaque string. Hand it to the app and nothing else: never log it or store it.

expiresAt.description: When it stops working: twenty-four hours from minting, with no refresh.

expiresInSeconds.description: The same, as seconds from this answer, at least 1: measure it on the client's own monotonic clock, never against `expiresAt` and the device's date.

Session.description: A session for one user, minted by the server plane.

SendResult.description: The message as stored, and its ticket after it.

messages.description: Ascending by `(createdAt, id)` whichever way was asked. Merge by `id`.

anyOf.description: An opaque cursor this server minted. Send it back as it came; one the server did not mint is `400 invalid_cursor`.

olderCursor.description: Send as `before` for the page before this one; null at the start of the thread.

newerCursor.description: Send as `after` to poll for newer messages. Never null, and unchanged when nothing is new; a full page means ask again at once.

unreadTotal.description: The team's unread messages across all of the user's tickets, for a badge.

pollAfterSeconds.description: Seconds to wait before the next poll of this thread, at least 1. Obey it.

MessagesPage.description: A page of a ticket's messages.

tickets.description: Newest first, by `(lastMessageAt, id)`. Merge by `id`: a ticket that moves can appear twice.

anyOf.description: An opaque cursor this server minted. Send it back as it came; one the server did not mint is `400 invalid_cursor`.

olderCursor.description: Send as `before` for the next, older page; null at the end of the list.

unreadTotal.description: The team's unread messages across all of the user's tickets, for a badge.

pollAfterSeconds.description: Seconds to wait before re-reading the first page, at least 1. Obey it.

TicketsPage.description: A page of the user's tickets. It has no `after`: a ticket with a new message moves to the top, so the list is polled by re-reading its first page.

unreadTotal.description: The team's unread messages across all of the user's tickets, after this.

ReadResult.description: The ticket after marking it read, and the new badge.

url.description: A short-lived link to the file's bytes on another host. Use it at once; never log it, store it or send the session's bearer to it. A `403` from it means ask again.

expiresInSeconds.description: How long the link works for, from this answer: at least 1.

version.description: The date of the newest line in the changelog, `docs/myblu-api-changelog.md`.

OpenApiDocument.description: This document: the OpenAPI 3.1 contract of the server answering.

ErrorCode.description: Why the request was refused. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know: a client classifies a code it does not know by the HTTP status it came with.

FileRefusalReason.description: On `file_refused`: `too_many` files, one `too_large`, all of them `too_large_total`, a `type` the server does not carry, or an `empty` file. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know.

message.description: A sentence in English for a developer's log. Never shown to the user, and never parsed.

field.description: On `invalid_request`, when one field is to blame: its name, as the request spelled it (a body field, a query parameter, a header).

filename.description: On `file_refused`: the file refused, or null when the refusal is about all of them.

WebhookEventType.description: The event's type, also in `X-ShipBlu-Event`. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know.

version.description: The body's shape: `1` on every event `/api/v1` sends.

id.description: The event, `<type>:<subject id>`, the same on every attempt. Dedupe on it for a day: an event can arrive more than once.

occurredAt.description: When the thing it reports happened, not when this attempt was sent.

externalId.description: The ticket's user, as the backend minted them.

type.description: A message from the team on one of the user's tickets.

message.description: The message, by id. Its text is never in the webhook.

MessageCreatedEvent.description: Sent when the team writes to the user: a person's reply or an automated one.

version.description: The body's shape: `1` on every event `/api/v1` sends.

id.description: The event, `<type>:<subject id>`, the same on every attempt. Dedupe on it for a day: an event can arrive more than once.

occurredAt.description: When the thing it reports happened, not when this attempt was sent.

externalId.description: The ticket's user, as the backend minted them.

type.description: A survey is waiting on one of the user's tickets.

expiresAt.description: When it can no longer be answered; null when it does not lapse.

SurveyCreatedEvent.description: Sent when a resolved ticket's survey is ready. From the survey's stage (stage 8).

version.description: The body's shape: `1` on every event `/api/v1` sends.

id.description: The event, `<type>:<subject id>`, the same on every attempt. Dedupe on it for a day: an event can arrive more than once.

occurredAt.description: When the thing it reports happened, not when this attempt was sent.

externalId.description: The ticket's user, as the backend minted them.

type.description: The event's type: one `WebhookEventType` names, or one added since.

AnyWebhookEvent.description: Any event, by the fields every type carries: what a receiver reads of a type it does not know, and answers `2xx` without acting on.

WebhookEvent.description: One event, by `type`. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know: a receiver answers 2xx to a type it does not know and does nothing with it. Such an event matches `AnyWebhookEvent`, the last arm, which every event matches.

sb_v.description: `"1"`. A payload without it is not ours.

sb_type.description: The webhook event's `type`. Values are added without notice, and a client must accept one it does not know.

sb_event_id.description: The webhook event's `id`. The app hands a client the same push when it arrives and again when it is tapped: the client answers the ticket both times, and fetches for an `id` only the first time.

sb_user.description: The webhook's `user.externalId`. A client ignores a push for any user but the one signed in.

PushData.description: The data keys myBlu's backend puts on the push it sends for each webhook event, every value a string. `push.handle` ignores any other key on the payload it is handed, such as one the app adds to a notification it draws itself.

Locale.description: The language the user wrote in: exactly `ar` or `en`.

Platform.description: The platform the app runs on.

RevokeReason.description: `signed_out` everywhere; `phone_changed`; `account_deleted`; `number_released`, the number now somebody else's; or `other`. With `account_deleted` or `number_released` the user's tickets also leave the app for good.

ExternalUserId.description: The user's id on myBlu's backend: 1 to 128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`, stable for a person, never reused for another, and never the phone number.

Phone.description: The phone number the backend verified, in strict E.164 with its plus: `+201001234567`, never the national `01001234567`.

TrackingNumber.description: A tracking number the ticket is about, as the app shows it: 1 to 64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 -`. Stored as sent and returned to this user only.

name.description: The user's name, used only when this creates the contact; a name the contact already has is never overwritten. At most 200 UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts: `maxLength` counts characters, as Python's `len` does, so a name with emoji in it can pass that and still be refused `400 invalid_request`.

client.description: The app the session is for.

CreateSessionRequest.description: Mint a session for one user.

RevokeSessionsRequest.description: End every session of one user, on every device.

text.description: What the user wrote. Required in JSON; blank is `400 empty_message`, and over the limit `400 invalid_request`, never cut short. At most 5000 UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts and `limits.messageMaxChars` states. `maxLength` counts characters, so a text with emoji in it can pass that and still be refused.

CreateTicketRequest.description: Open a ticket with its first message.

text.description: What the user wrote; may be empty or left out when there is a file. At most 5000 UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts and `limits.messageMaxChars` states. `maxLength` counts characters, so a text with emoji in it can pass that and still be refused.

files.description: Repeated, one part per file in the order to show them. Each part carries its filename and a `Content-Type` from `GET /config`; one with none, or `application/octet-stream`, is admitted by its extension.

CreateTicketMultipart.description: Open a ticket with files. Accepted from the files stage; before it, a multipart body is `400 invalid_request`. `Content-Length` is required (`411` without it).

text.description: What the user wrote. Required in JSON; blank is `400 empty_message`, and over the limit `400 invalid_request`, never cut short. At most 5000 UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts and `limits.messageMaxChars` states. `maxLength` counts characters, so a text with emoji in it can pass that and still be refused.

SendMessageRequest.description: Send a message on a ticket.

text.description: What the user wrote; may be empty or left out when there is a file. At most 5000 UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts and `limits.messageMaxChars` states. `maxLength` counts characters, so a text with emoji in it can pass that and still be refused.

files.description: Repeated, one part per file in the order to show them. Each part carries its filename and a `Content-Type` from `GET /config`; one with none, or `application/octet-stream`, is admitted by its extension.

SendMessageMultipart.description: Send a message with files. Accepted from the files stage; before it, a multipart body is `400 invalid_request`. `Content-Length` is required (`411` without it).

upTo.description: The newest message on screen: any message this API returned on this ticket, the user's own included. Marking twice, or backwards, changes nothing.

MarkReadRequest.description: Mark the team's messages read, up to one.

rating.description: 1 to 5. Posted when tapped; the first rating wins.

comment.description: A comment, sent as a second `POST` carrying the same rating. Over the limit is `400 invalid_request`, never cut short. At most 2000 UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's `length` counts and `survey.commentMaxChars` states. `maxLength` counts characters, so a text with emoji in it can pass that and still be refused.

serverPlane.description: `MYBLU_API_TOKEN`, held by myBlu's backend and never shipped in an app: a value compiled into a binary is extractable, and whoever extracts it can mint any user. It mints and ends sessions; nothing else accepts it.

clientPlane.description: A session token for one user, minted by the server plane and handed to the app by myBlu's backend. Twenty-four hours from minting, with no refresh: on any `401` the SDK asks for a new one once and replays once.

webhookSignature.name: X-ShipBlu-Signature
webhookSignature.description: `v1=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256, under `MYBLU_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, of `<X-ShipBlu-Timestamp>.<raw body>`. Verify over the raw bytes, before parsing; refuse a timestamp more than five minutes off.

ShipBluClient.name: ShipBlu-Client
ShipBluClient.description: Required on every client-plane request: `name/version` tokens separated by spaces, the SDK first, e.g. `sdk-ts/0.3.0 app/5.4.1 ios/18.1`. A request without it is `400 invalid_request`; an SDK or app this server no longer serves is `426 client_upgrade_required`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Required on the two requests that write a message: a UUID the client makes before the first attempt and sends again, unchanged, on every retry of that send.

TicketIdPath.name: id
TicketIdPath.description: A ticket the signed-in user opened. Anything else is `404 not_found`.

AttachmentIdPath.name: id
AttachmentIdPath.description: An attachment on one of the signed-in user's tickets. Anything else is `404 not_found`.

WebhookEvent.name: X-ShipBlu-Event
WebhookEvent.description: The body's `type`, so a receiver can route before it parses.

WebhookTimestamp.name: X-ShipBlu-Timestamp
WebhookTimestamp.description: Unix seconds when this attempt was signed: a retry carries its own. Refuse one more than five minutes from the receiver's clock.

WebhookSignature.name: X-ShipBlu-Signature
WebhookSignature.description: `v1=` and the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, under the shared secret, of the `X-ShipBlu-Timestamp` value, a `.`, and the raw body. While a secret is rotated, two of them separated by a comma; accept the request when either matches.

RequestId.description: On every answer: an opaque id for this request, repeated in an error body. Quote it in a bug report.

CacheControl.description: On every answer: nothing this API returns may be cached by anything between it and the app.

IdempotentReplayed.description: On a `200` that answers a retried send: the message was stored by an earlier attempt under the same key, and this is what it stored.

RetryAfter.description: On a `429`: whole seconds to wait before asking again.

invalid_request.summary: A field the request got wrong

invalid_cursor.summary: A cursor this server did not mint

error.message: The cursor was not minted by this server.
Idempotency-Key is required on this request, and must be a UUID.
A message needs words or a file.

unauthenticated.summary: No live session for this bearer

error.message: No live session for this bearer.

blocked.summary: A user who may not use support

error.message: This user may not use support.

not_found.summary: Not the user's, or not there

error.message: No such ticket for this user.

ticket_closed.summary: A reply to a closed ticket

error.message: The ticket is closed; open a new one.
This user has 10 open or pending tickets.

key_reused.summary: A key sent with another request

error.message: This Idempotency-Key was used for another request.

length_required.summary: A multipart body without its length

error.message: A multipart body must carry Content-Length.
The body is larger than 27262976 bytes.

client_upgrade_required.summary: An SDK this server no longer serves

error.message: sdk-ts/0.0.9 is no longer served; update the SDK.
Too many requests; wait for Retry-After.
Something failed on the server. The request id names it in the log.

upload_failed.summary: A file that could not be stored

error.message: A file could not be stored, so nothing was. Retry the whole send under the same key.
The API is not switched on here.
